subject: MedSecure private deployment blueprint — recap & next milestones
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Markovic <elena.markovic@medsecure.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: MedSecure private deployment blueprint — recap & next milestones

Hi Elena,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the clarity around MedSecure's constraints. Below is a concise recap of the call so we have aligned expectations and clear next actions. Please flag anything I missed or mischaracterized.

TL;DR (what you asked for)
- Private/on-prem or VPC-hosted inference for PHI workflows with no egress of raw patient data.
- Customer-managed KMS (HSM preferred) and audit-ready key rotation.
- Air-gap option for offline model updates is a hard requirement for some facilities.
- Strict outbound firewall rules: only allow specific IPs and limited external endpoints.

Pain points you described
1) Current vendor has unpredictable latency and token cost spikes during batch jobs — impacting throughput SLAs.
2) Security team needs demonstrable separation of telemetry and strict KMS control.
3) Procurement needs a clear deployment blueprint and an initial fixed-cost estimate to move to RFP.

Current stack (as discussed)
- Model hosting: internal GPU cluster (NVIDIA A100) for non-production workloads
- Data plane: VPC with segmented subnets; some sites are air-gapped (no inbound/outbound internet)
- Identity & secrets: HashiCorp Vault (on-prem) for secrets, current KMS is CloudKMS (but must be replaced/extended with customer-managed HSM)

Success criteria (how MedSecure will consider a pilot successful)
- Latency: 99th percentile inference latency <= 300ms at 512 tokens for interactive paths.
- Cost: Predictable per-token unit economics within +/-15% of our pilot estimate.
- Security: Keys are customer-managed; full audit log for all inference requests; data is never stored outside your VPC unless explicitly allowed.
- Operations: Can do rolling upgrades with automated fallback and clear rollback plan.

Constraints and special requirements
- Several hospital sites operate in air-gap mode: model updates must be staged on removable media or via an approved appliance process.
- Outbound egress only to the three Redwood collector IPs we will provide; all other outbound blocked at perimeter.
- SOC 2 and HIPAA controls required; customer will need artifact-level evidence during procurement.

Attachments shared (drafts)
- medsecure_network_constraints.pdf (network/NAT/firewall checklist)
- redwood_private-blueprint-summary.xlsx (deployment steps + estimated effort)
- SOC2-evidence-pack.pdf (SOC 2 high-level artifacts we can provide)

Proposed next steps (owners & dates)
1) Redwood: deliver an expanded network diagram and a short checklist for air-gap model delivery (Jonas) — target: 2027-04-07.
2) MedSecure: share the list of allowed outbound IPs and any existing HSM vendor details (Elena / IT Ops) — target: 2027-04-08.
3) Joint: schedule a 60-minute technical workshop with your security + networking team to walk the blueprint and validate constraints (Aisha to coordinate) — target meeting week of 2027-04-12.
4) Procurement: after workshop, we will produce a fixed-scope pilot SOW + Ballpark pricing (Redwood) — target: 2027-04-15.

Questions we still have
- For air-gapped sites, do you have a preferred appliance vendor or process for delivering large model binaries?
- Is Vault going to be the canonical secrets store in pilot, or do you need Redwood to integrate directly with an HSM (PKCS#11) only?

If this captures everything, I'll go ahead and: (a) attach an expanded network diagram and (b) send a calendar proposal for the workshop.

Thanks,

Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124

Subject: Re: MedSecure private deployment blueprint — recap & next milestones

Jonas — thanks for the clear recap. This aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from the security side:

- Firewall/egress: our perimeter team will only allow outbound to whitelisted IPs. We will provide the list but note the change management window is 48–72 hours.
- HSM: we currently operate an on-prem Thales HSM for production keys; for pilot we can provide a vault-backed key but ultimate requirement is HSM (PKCS#11).
- Air-gap: some clinics accept shipping encrypted model bundles on encrypted SSDs; others require a portable appliance with a USB transfer process and chain-of-custody logging.

Action for us: we will validate which clinic sites require strict air-gap vs. limited-offline transfer and share a site categorization by 2027-04-08.

Request: could you expand the network diagram to show NAT translation points and the expected egress ports/protocols (we need that for our firewall change request)? Also include the minimal list of endpoints Redwood needs to reach for telemetry/metrics if any.

Thanks — Elena
Elena Markovic
VP, Security & Compliance | MedSecure Health
elena.markovic@medsecure.com

- Required outbound ports (TCP 443 for limited telemetry; we can operate telemetry over an enterprise collector inside your VPC to avoid direct outbound)

- HSM integration: we will validate support for Thales PKCS#11 in our pilot runner. If needed, Redwood can ship a pre-provisioned appliance image that your on-prem team can load and connect to HSM for key management.
- Air-gap delivery: we propose two delivery modes: encrypted SSD with signed manifest OR a physical appliance update. We'll outline both in the workshop and provide a runbook.

Proposed workshop times (all PT):
- Tue 2027-04-13 10:00–11:00
- Wed 2027-04-14 13:00–14:00
Please confirm which works for security+networking. Aisha, can you send the invite once Elena confirms?

I'll also prepare the pilot SOW template and a short checklist for procurement to review.

Best,
